principle_violations.reason: Multiple classes are shouldering multiple responsibilities like managing orders, processing payments, and handling authentication separately but aren't entirely adhering to the SRP principle since authentication logic is within payment processors.
principle_violations.suggestion: Refactor the payment processing to separate the authentication responsibility into its own class, distinct from the payment processing logic. Ensure each class addresses only one responsibility.

principle_violations.reason: The DebitCardPaymentProcessor class ties a concrete authorizer in its implementation, which makes adding new types of authorization without modifying the class difficult.
principle_violations.suggestion: Introduce an interface for authorization and allow the payment processor class to work with any objects that implement this interface, avoiding modifications when new authorization schemes need to be integrated.

principle_violations.reason: The DebitCardPaymentProcessor class depends on a concrete class SMSAuthorizer. It should depend on an abstraction to follow the dependency inversion principle.
principle_violations.suggestion: Define an interface for the Authorizer and let the DebitCardPaymentProcessor depend on this interface.
